argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than the audited claim. The admissible record does not support treating the 6% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring as substitutes for the policy predicate. It does support a limited certification rationale based on aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, reversibility, and a disclosure-dependent deployment posture, while expressly acknowledging that the small-business onboarding segment remains below target and exposed. The packet should therefore be read as caveated certification with explicit disclosure and monitoring obligations, not as clean proof that the weakness is cured or fully mitigated by rollout controls alone.
claims_about_policy: The admissible policy text cuts against any claim that rollout controls alone satisfy governance here: the affected use case was not excluded, and the existing risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not address the exposed segment. At the same time, the admissible evidence supports a narrower policy-consistent framing: certification can only be defended as conditional and caveated, with the material limitation expressly disclosed for the named launch use case and monitored through deployment. Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance supports that disclosure-and-monitoring posture, but does not by itself convert this into clean compliance.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not the only proportionate response on this record. The rollout is limited to 6%, reversible, and supported by monitoring, while aggregate readiness cleared by 2.1 percentage points and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents. Given those controls, remaining uncertainty can be handled through a caveated certification posture rather than treating the record as if it supported an unrestricted launch certification.
concessions: The small-business onboarding segment is below target on long-context onboarding support and remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate is random by account and does not exclude the affected use case.
The current risk-acceptance draft is incomplete because the approver line is blank and it does not mention small-business onboarding exposure.
The admissible record does not prove that required launch disclosure has already been completed in an approved model-card artifact.
The record does not support a claim of clean compliance based on rollout controls alone.
